items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: single-detached housing sits on fee-simple lots on the residential streets east and north of downtown under RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%. Those are the zone's subdivision minimums, not a claim that every existing lot meets them. Town Centre parcels carry Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same bylaw.
Bare-land strata: there are a few scattered lots, but no named community. On a bare-land strata lot, you own a strata lot, pay strata fees and follow the bylaws, and the Form B is the key document.

These are policy designations over largely built parcels — any assembly is a private negotiation over built lots, not a listed vacant-land offering. The City names a downtown location "Brickwater" at 11897 227 Street, but official City pages do not state its building type or developer.

items.t: Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; Dewdney Trunk Road east–west through downtown and the neighbourhoods to the east; 224 Street and 226 Street north–south through the downtown core; and the Haney Bypass, linking Lougheed Highway to Port Haney at the southwest corner.

Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in this area, served by routes including the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791. The R3 Lougheed Highway RapidBus runs from Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place, and Port Haney Station (22300 River Road, at the southwest corner) has weekday West Coast Express trains between Waterfront and Mission City.

Schools in the area: Golden Ears Elementary (K–7), 23124 118 Avenue; Harry Hooge Elementary (K–7), 12280 230 Street; Thomas Haney Secondary (7–12), 23000 116 Avenue; ci:tməxw Environmental Community (K–8), 23125 116 Avenue; and District 42 Alternative Secondary (9–12), 23125 116 Avenue. SD42 has no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary 8–12, with Thomas Haney starting at Grade 7.

Civic centre: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place); Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, surrounded by City Hall, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, The ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, with the Cenotaph, bandstand and Haney Farmers Market; Maple Ridge Public Library (130–22470 Dewdney Trunk Road), the city's only library; and Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre in Haney Place Mall (121–11900 Haney Place, open 7 days, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.). Ridge Meadows Hospital (11666 Laity Street, with 24/7 emergency care) is just west of the area.

items.t: Density policy is the land story here, not vacant lots. The Town Centre Core designation, the two Transit-Oriented Areas (Bylaw No. 8001-2024), the adopted Lougheed Transit Corridor (Bylaw No. 7781-2021, adopted Jan 27, 2026, ending at 221 St) and the Albion Area Plan adoption (Oct 28, 2025) all push value into assemblies and added units on built lots — pricing a teardown on today's single-house use alone misses the documented direction, and pricing it as if rezoning were assured overpays for a designation, not an approval.

There are no separate figures for land: the board reports detached homes and condos and townhomes only. Maple Ridge's medians that month were $1,131,000 for detached homes and $525,000 for condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure — the buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata bylaws, and diligence runs through the Form B, exactly as with any strata; what differs is that the lot itself is bare land / a detached-house lot rather than a unit in a shared building envelope.
Confirm the plan number, lot count and fee for a bare-land strata lot here on the title and Form B.

blocks.text: Land assemblies / development sites

items.t: Town Centre Core and River Bend are plan designations, not sites for sale. The Town Centre Area Plan update added River Bend, simplified the land use designations and added a Town Centre Core designation allowing higher density downtown around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station, both transit-oriented areas under Bylaw No. 8001-2024. These cover mostly built lots, so any land assembly is a private deal over existing homes, not vacant land for sale.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near East Central lots

items.t: The City doesn't publish a boundary for the board's "East Central" area. The Town Centre Area Plan covers the downtown core on the west side, expanded to include River Bend, and the rest of the area takes in the streets east and north of downtown toward 232 Street and 124 Avenue.

Schools in the area: Golden Ears Elementary (K–7), 23124 118 Avenue; Harry Hooge Elementary (K–7), 12280 230 Street; Thomas Haney Secondary (7–12), 23000 116 Avenue; ci:tməxw Environmental Community (K–8), 23125 116 Avenue; and District 42 Alternative Secondary (9–12), 23125 116 Avenue. Catchments are set by address; SD42 has no middle schools (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Central

items.t: The Lougheed Transit Corridor plan was adopted January 27, 2026 (Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021, after a public hearing on January 20). The corridor runs along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road from the city's west boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street.

Albion Area Plan: adopted Oct 28, 2025 as part of the City's fall 2025 OCP/area-plan update series (Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion) — Albion is east of this sub-area, but the same update series is the planning context for East Central's Town Centre changes.

Suites and extra units: one secondary suite per lot, inside the house, up to 40% of its floor area, and not in the floodplain area. Eligible single-family and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's small-scale housing rules. Subdividing an RS-1 lot still needs the minimum 668.0 m² lot, 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep; extra units don't create new lots.

On a bare-land strata lot, BC strata rules apply: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited by bylaw), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.

I don't know of any ALR land here. If there were: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm tax status, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

Pricing a teardown on its current single-house use alone misses that, but paying as if a rezoning were certain means paying for a plan designation, not an approval.

Civic centre: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place); Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, surrounded by City Hall, the ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, with the Cenotaph, bandstand and Haney Farmers Market; Maple Ridge Public Library (130–22470 Dewdney Trunk Road), the city's only library; and Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre in Haney Place Mall (121–11900 Haney Place, open 7 days, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.).
Hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, is the community hospital for Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows with 24/7 emergency care, west of this sub-area.

Heritage at the southwest corner: Port Haney was historically the steamboat landing and CPR station for the area, and the Bandstand in Memorial Peace Park was presented by the Maple Ridge Concert Band as a gift to the people of Maple Ridge — the oldest land in this sub-area carries heritage context a teardown buyer should check before assuming a clean rebuild.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in East Central

items.t: Zoning (Bylaw No. 7600-2019): houses are mostly RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), with a minimum lot of 668.0 m², 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep, and up to 40% coverage. Town Centre properties have commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same bylaw.

Floodplain and escarpment: the south edge (River Road and Port Haney) is along the Fraser River. There, the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including a safety margin), a covenant on title notes floodplain construction, no living space can be below that level on affected lots, and suites aren't allowed on floodplain properties. The Fraser River Escarpment policy area reaches the area's west edge (its east boundary is 224 Street); lots within 300 m of the escarpment crest need a geotechnical report, registered in a covenant, before a building permit. blocks.text: East Central: streets and boundaries

items.t: East Central sits east of West Central and the Town Centre seam at 222–224 Street, west of Cottonwood, with Southwest Maple Ridge (Port Haney) at its southwest corner and Albion further east along Lougheed Highway; residents and the City usually call its west end Downtown Maple Ridge, Haney, or the Town Centre.

blocks.text: East Central: the homes

items.t: This sub-area holds two stocks side by side: freehold single-detached houses on the residential streets east and north of downtown, and strata condos concentrated in the Town Centre core along 224 Street, 226 Street, 227 Street and 121 Avenue.

The condo cluster exists because the plan allows it: the Town Centre Core designation supports higher densities in a transit-oriented downtown anchored by the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station.
The City names a downtown location "Brickwater" at 11897 227 Street.

blocks.text: East Central: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Town Centre Area Plan update expanded the plan boundaries to incorporate River Bend, consolidated the land use designations, and added a Town Centre Core designation supporting higher densities around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station.

Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 covers the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station transit-oriented areas inside this plan area, which changes the parking and density rules a downtown buyer or builder meets.
Town Centre parcels carry Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, separate from the house zones on the residential streets.

blocks.text: East Central: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Memorial Peace Park, on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, is surrounded by City Hall, the Leisure Centre, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, The ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, holds the Cenotaph and the Bandstand, and hosts the Haney Farmers Market — downtown condos face event and market activity, not just retail.
The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre at 11925 Haney Place, at the west edge of this sub-area, has an indoor pool, fitness centre, gymnasium and sport courts.
Maple Ridge Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road is inside this sub-area and is the only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Maple Ridge.

The Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is inside Haney Place Mall at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Ridge Meadows Hospital itself is west of this sub-area at 11666 Laity Street.
Port Haney, at the sub-area's southwest corner, was historically the steamboat landing and Canadian Pacific Railway station for the area.

blocks.text: East Central: development and new projects

items.t: Status: adopted plan update as described on the City's plan page (as of November 3, 2026).

Langley–Haney Place Bus Rapid Transit, TransLink: 22 kilometres between Willowbrook and Haney Place with peak service every 10 minutes, ending at the Haney Transit Exchange in this sub-area; designs, costs and timelines are not yet determined. Status: detailed planning (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: East Central: getting around

items.t: Haney Place Exchange is in this sub-area; routes on TransLink's Haney Place route diagram include the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791, and the 733 serves the residential area north of downtown.
Port Haney Station at 22300 River Road, at the sub-area's southwest corner, runs West Coast Express trains on weekdays between Waterfront Station (downtown Vancouver) and Mission City.

Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) runs along the south side, Dewdney Trunk Road runs east–west through downtown, 224 Street and 226 Street are the main north–south streets through the core, and the Haney Bypass links Lougheed Highway to Port Haney at the southwest corner.
